Q1: The British. A Union Jack flies over the fortified tower on the rock (frames 40-41, Jan 1780). The pictures never show who the besiegers are.
Q2: '1779 — The Great Siege', a caption in frame 23 (21 Jun 1779). It is a siege of the Rock: soldiers and cannons are massed on the land side (frames 27-33), and ships gather in the bay (frames 34-39).
Q3: Not sure. The pictures suggest the town is blockaded by land and sea, since enemy ships sit in the bay and troops are camped on the plain. No frame shows food shortage or starving people.
Q4: Ships arrive on the water around the town (frame 47, 18 Jan 1780, and frames 53-56, Apr 1781). They look like a relief fleet, and a ship also arrives at the harbour in frame 52. Nothing shows what is on board or whose ships they are. In frames 57-59 there is night fire and a burst on the town, so the Apr 1781 ships may be firing on it instead.
